## Finding

With `--model-huge` the compiler stops when it compiles a comparison of two function addresses,
such as `&f1 != &g1`. On r17158 with `-c --model-huge` the message is `FATAL Compiler Internal
Error in file 'src/mcs51/gen.c' line number '2077' : need pointerCode`. In trunk a guard that names
this ticket disables both assertions of `tests/funcptrcmp.c.in` for every mcs51 model.

## Cause

With `--model-huge`, functions are banked unless they are declared `__nonbanked`, and their
addresses have three bytes. `opIsGptr` in `src/mcs51/gen.c` returns true for these addresses. For
them `gencjneshort` and `genCmp` emit pushes of the right operand, call `loadDptrFromOperand` with
`loadBToo` set for the left operand, and emit a call to `sdcc_gptr_cmp`. For an immediate operand,
`loadDptrFromOperand` has code that loads B only when the operand is the result of a cast
(`from_cast_remat`). For the address of a function it reaches the assertion with the message
`need pointerCode`.

## Fix

For an immediate operand whose type is a banked function, `loadDptrFromOperand` loads B with the
third byte of the address, which is the bank. `aopGet` returns `#(name >> 16)` for that byte, and
the code that pushes the right operand uses this form too. The patch also removes the guard from
`tests/funcptrcmp.c.in`.

## Verification

After the guard is removed, `tests/funcptrcmp.c.in` does not compile for mcs51-huge without the
patch. With the patch it passes for every mcs51 regression target except mcs51-xstack-auto, which
was not run. Functions declared `__banked` in the other models were not tested.
